subject: biology
title: Protein synthesis
key_idea: Proteins are made in two stages. In **transcription**, the gene in the nucleus is copied into mRNA. In **translation**, a ribosome reads the mRNA and tRNA brings the amino acids, which join in order to make the protein.

blocks.text: A gene is a code for a protein. This section covers the key words and the order of events.

items.meaning: Messenger RNA. A copy of a gene that carries the code from the nucleus to a ribosome.
Copying a gene from DNA into mRNA, in the nucleus.
Reading the mRNA at a ribosome and building a protein from amino acids.
Transfer RNA. A carrier molecule that brings a specific amino acid to the ribosome.
The structure in the cytoplasm where proteins are made.

diagram.alt: Put the stages of protein synthesis in order.
steps: The DNA unwinds (unzips) around the gene
A copy of the gene is made as mRNA (transcription)
The mRNA leaves the nucleus and goes to a ribosome
tRNA molecules bring the amino acid for each triplet of the mRNA (translation)
The amino acids are joined into a chain
The chain folds up into the specific protein

items: Transcription makes mRNA in the nucleus.
Translation makes the protein at a ribosome.
The DNA stays in the nucleus. The mRNA carries the code out.

blocks.text: Transcription copies one gene into mRNA. It happens in the nucleus.

items: The DNA helix unwinds (unzips) around the gene. The strands separate.
An enzyme called **RNA polymerase** binds to the DNA, at the start of the gene.
It builds a strand of mRNA, a chain of nucleotides, using one DNA strand as the template.
The mRNA bases are **complementary** to the DNA bases, so the mRNA carries a copy of the code.
mRNA has the base **U** (uracil) instead of T. So A pairs with U.

items.text: The strand that is copied reads G G T G C A T A T.
G pairs with C, C with G and T with A. A pairs with U, not T.
The mRNA reads C C A C G U A U A.

items: RNA polymerase makes mRNA from a gene.
mRNA is complementary to the DNA and has U in place of T.
mRNA then leaves the nucleus.

blocks.text: Translation happens at a ribosome in the cytoplasm. The mRNA is the code, and tRNA brings the parts.

items: The mRNA binds to a **ribosome**.
The ribosome reads the mRNA in groups of three bases (triplets or codons).
Each triplet codes for **one amino acid**.
**tRNA** molecules carry specific amino acids. Each tRNA has an anticodon that pairs with its codon.
The amino acids are joined by peptide bonds into a chain, a polypeptide.
The chain folds into the specific shape of the protein.

blocks.label: Maximum number of amino acids coded for
where: number of bases in the coding strand
three bases code for one amino acid
blocks.formula: number of amino acids = number of bases ÷ 3

items.text: A strand reads T T G A T T G C G T A A. There are 12 bases.
12 ÷ 3 = 4. It codes for at most 4 amino acids.

items: A change of one base gives a different set of three bases.
That can code for a different amino acid, so the mRNA and the protein change.
A different amino acid can change the shape of the protein, for example an enzyme's active site.
The substrate may then no longer fit, so the enzyme cannot work.
Translation needs mRNA, a ribosome, tRNA and amino acids.
Three bases code for one amino acid.
A change in the code can change the protein's shape and stop it working.

checks.q: Name the stage of protein synthesis that makes mRNA, and say where it happens.
Describe the job of tRNA in making a protein.
checks.a: tRNA is a carrier molecule. It brings a specific amino acid to the ribosome, matching each triplet of the mRNA.

checks.q: A DNA strand reads A C G T. Write the mRNA copied from it.

worked_example.question:
Adult Himalayan rabbits have white fur over most of the body and black fur on the nose, ears and feet. The black fur is caused by a substance called melanin, which is made from tyrosine by the enzyme tyrosinase.

White rabbits have one base change in the gene that codes for the enzyme tyrosinase.

Explain how a change of one base in the DNA of the gene coding for tyrosinase could stop the tyrosinase working.
answer_points: It gives a different set of 3 bases (a different triplet).
This codes for a different amino acid.
Which alters the shape of the enzyme's active site.
So the tyrosine (substrate) no longer fits, and enzyme-substrate complexes cannot form.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each link in the chain: base, triplet, amino acid, active site, substrate.

worked_example.question:
The genetic material from the virus is transcribed by the plant cell.

Describe how mRNA is produced during transcription.
answer_points: The DNA helix unwinds (unzips, the strands separate).
RNA polymerase (the enzyme) binds to the non-coding region (the promoter).
The mRNA strand is complementary: it is a chain of nucleotides joined together.
It contains U instead of T, so A pairs with U.
worked_example.tip: Any four of the five points score. Name the enzyme, and give the base difference.

worked_example.question:
Protein synthesis takes place inside cells.

Describe what happens during protein synthesis.

Use terms from the list in your answer.

amino acids   DNA   mRNA   transcription   translation   ribosome
answer_points: The DNA unwinds (unzips).
During transcription mRNA is made.
The mRNA moves from the nucleus to the cytoplasm (ribosomes).
Translation happens on the ribosomes.
tRNA (carrier molecules) bring specific amino acids.
The amino acids are joined to form a protein.
worked_example.tip: Any four of the six points score. Do not say that amino acids are produced.

worked_example.question:
Proteins are biological molecules.
Explain how proteins are made.
answer_points: Messenger RNA (mRNA) is a copy of a gene (DNA).
The mRNA is made in the nucleus.
The gene (DNA) stays in the nucleus.
The mRNA moves to the cytoplasm.
The mRNA passes through a ribosome.
The ribosome assembles amino acids into a polypeptide (protein).
The sequence of amino acids is determined by the sequence of bases in the mRNA.
worked_example.tip: Any six points score the six marks. Cover where the mRNA is made, where it goes and what the ribosome does.

blocks.text: (Supplement) DNA controls what a cell does by controlling which proteins it makes.

items: The sequence of amino acids decides the **shape** of the protein, and the shape decides what it can do.
The proteins include **enzymes**, membrane carriers and receptors for neurotransmitters.
Most body cells in an organism have the same genes.
Many genes in a cell are not **expressed**. The cell makes only the specific proteins it needs.

worked_example.question:
Amylase is a protein.

Describe how protein is made in a cell.
answer_points: Transcription: the gene is copied into mRNA.
The mRNA leaves the nucleus and enters the cytoplasm.
The mRNA binds to a ribosome.
tRNA brings the amino acids, each attached to its tRNA.
Codons on the mRNA pair with anticodons (complementary bases) on the tRNA.
Translation: the amino acids join into a chain (polypeptide).
worked_example.tip: Any five points score the five marks. Use the words transcription, translation, codon and anticodon.

items: RNA is **single stranded**. DNA has two strands.
RNA contains **uracil (U)** instead of thymine (T).
A change in the DNA base sequence changes the mRNA codons, the tRNA anticodons and the amino acids. This can change the protein and so the phenotype.
